name: Widely-known facts, recorded without a single citable registry
note: The deliberate relaxation of this project's strictest rule, recorded here so nobody
mistakes it for an oversight.
Everything else in the corpus is either fetched from a pinned source or invented, and
the two are kept apart because the first can be checked and the second cannot be
wrong. This file is neither. `Otter` is a real animal, `Kilimanjaro` is a real
mountain and `Toyota` is a real company -- so there IS a fact of the matter, which is
what got these categories refused for months -- but no registry publishes `the list of
animals a fake-data library should offer`, and the ones that come closest are either
share-alike, taxonomic rather than colloquial, or both.
So these were written from general knowledge, and the honest description of their
accuracy is: high, but unverified and unverifiable by this pipeline. A wrong entry
here is a wrong entry, not a licence problem -- it will read oddly in a fixture and
somebody will correct it in a diff. That is a weaker guarantee than every other
adapter offers, and it is why this is a separate source rather than more rows under
`decoy-authored`, which claims to be original content and would be lying about these.
`public-facts` rather than Apache-2.0 for the same reason `iana-tld` carries it: the
content is facts about the world, which nobody owns. The selection and arrangement
are this project's and are covered by the repository licence.
Trademarks appear -- car makers, camera makers, universities, football clubs. Naming
a trademark to refer to the thing it names is nominative use and is not what trademark
law restricts; the restriction is on using a mark so as to suggest endorsement or
cause confusion in trade, which a fixture generator does not do. Decoy claims no
affiliation with any of them.
Living people appear in `notable.actor`, `notable.musician` and `notable.athlete`, and
that is the one category here worth a second thought. The project refuses rosters of
real people -- Pakistan's Gallup election database was declined on exactly that ground
-- and the distinction being drawn is between identifying private individuals, which
that database does, and naming public figures already known to everyone, which every
faker library does. The historical lists (philosophers, scientists, composers,
explorers) raise no such question at all.
English only, and no artifact, for the same reasons as `decoy-authored`.
